Virbalis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marijampolė County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Virbalis's Jews, from the mid-17th century, relied on the town's location near the German border for economic stability — trading in commerce and agriculture, and even smuggling immigrants across the border, much like the neighboring community of Kybartai, documented elsewhere in this collection, whose Jews were in fact buried in this very cemetery until 1912. The town maintained the United Company for Financial Credit for Jewish Agrarians and an organization specifically dedicated to aiding immigrants. On June 22, 1941, German forces entered Virbalis without resistance; over the following three months, the entire Jewish community was murdered in nearby anti-tank trenches, and only three women, hidden by Lithuanian families, survived. According to an ancient gravestone inscription, burials at this cemetery began in the early 18th century, and it is believed to sit on the site of an even earlier Jewish cemetery.
